transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is that... I just feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. It’s like the second I finish one thing, whether that's at school or at home, I immediately jump right into the next task. I just never seem to be able to shut myself off.
Have you always felt this way for as long as you can remember, or is this something that has started more recently?

Well, not my whole life, no. I mean, this specific level of trouble—where I just can't seem to stop at all—has really been going on for about eight months. That's... yeah, that's right around the time our older relative moved in with us, and it's just been like this ever since.
In addition to feeling like you're constantly running, have you felt persistently sad or lost interest in the things you usually enjoy over these past eight months?

No, I haven't felt sad. I mean, I still enjoy the things I usually do. I just... I do them at a hundred miles an hour now. But no, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or lost interest in anything like that.
Do you find that you are spending a significant amount of your time worrying about a variety of different things in your daily life, such as your schoolwork, your family, or your future?

No, not really. I mean, I have the normal everyday stress from teaching, but... no, I don't spend a lot of time worrying about things like that. I don't really sit around fretting about the future or my family. It's not that my mind is stuck on worries, it's just that I can't seem to physically settle down.
Since your relative moved in, have you found yourself acting out, behaving in ways that break rules, or having more conflicts with others than you used to?

No, I wouldn't say that. I'm not breaking any rules or getting into fights or anything. I mean, I might get a little impatient sometimes just because I can't sit still, but... no, I'm not acting out or having big conflicts with people. It's really just the physical restlessness.
Do you often experience physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling tense, or having aches and pains throughout your body?

No, I don't really have that. I mean, my muscles get a little tired sometimes just because I'm always moving around so much, but... no, I don't feel tense or have aches and pains like that. It's not a tight feeling, it's just... I just have to keep moving.
Looking back at your childhood or your teenage years, before this relative moved in, did you ever struggle with things like staying focused on tasks, losing things, or acting impulsively?

Yeah, definitely. This isn't something that just started with this family change. It's been a part of who I am long before adulthood. I mean, my mother actually used to joke that even back in elementary school, I taught the class from my seat. I was just always out of my chair, talking, or... or cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, yes, it's always been there.
When you think back to your childhood, were you more often criticized for being unable to pay attention and keep track of your things, or for being physically disruptive and unable to wait your turn?

It was definitely the physical stuff. Um, being disruptive and not waiting my turn. I don't really remember getting in trouble for losing my belongings or, you know, not paying attention. It was always just... "sit down," or "stop interrupting." That's what I heard the most.
Do you find that you have trouble waiting your turn or staying seated in your workplace or social settings just as much as you did back in school?

Yes, I definitely still struggle with staying seated. Whether I'm supposed to sit through a professional training, a school meeting, or even just dinner with the family, I... I just keep finding reasons to get up. I'll get up to refill my water, check the copier, or go look in on my relative. I just can't stay put, even when I know getting up like that makes me look disrespectful.
Do you find that you frequently make careless mistakes in your work or have trouble sustaining your focus on tasks that are not particularly interesting to you?

No, not really. I mean, I don't struggle with careless mistakes or losing focus on my work. As a special education teacher, I have to be pretty detailed with my paperwork and lesson plans, and I manage that fine. My issue is more about the physical restlessness, like I mentioned, not so much the attention or focus part of it.
